title: Tar Up the Logs
description: Bundle the five log files in /var/log/app into a single gzipped tarball in your home directory.
scenario: Support needs last week's staging logs attached to a ticket, but five separate files violate the attachment policy: everything must travel as ONE gzipped archive. Bundle /var/log/app into /home/intern/app-logs.tar.gz with tar, then prove the archive is intact by listing its contents.
symptoms: The ticketing system rejects multiple attachments
The archive must be gzip-compressed, not a plain tar
Nobody verified the last archive anyone sent — this one must be checked
mission: Create /home/intern/app-logs.tar.gz containing the five log files from /var/log/app, and verify it with `tar -tzf`.

hints.title: The three flags
hints.content: tar czf = **c**reate an archive, compress with g**z**ip, write to **f**ile. In that order: `tar -czf out.tar.gz paths...`.

hints.title: Control the paths inside
hints.content: `-C /var/log app` first cds to /var/log, then archives the app directory — so entries come out as app/app.log instead of absolute paths.

hints.title: Verify before sending
hints.content: `tar -tzf` (t = list) prints the contents without extracting. A truncated or corrupt archive fails here, not at the recipient's end.

acceptance_criteria.description: the file is a valid gzipped tar archive
